# An own-depth hypograph does not preserve actual critical cap budgets
volume on the concave own-depth hypograph. It is not an OC counterexample
or a claim about a minimum over all convex bodies. In particular the
critical-circuit multipliers below are not asserted to satisfy the full
variational boundary stress of such a minimum.

## 1. Actual source, with no heavy fiber

In one integer coordinate z and one continuous coordinate x, put

    L(z)=-11/20+|z|/20,
    U(z)=19/20-9|z|/20,
    C={(z,x):-1<=z<=1, L(z)<=x<=U(z)}.

This is a full-dimensional compact convex polygon, since L is convex
and U is concave. Its complete integer base is {-1,0,1}. The endpoint
fibers are [-1/2,1/2], and the middle fiber is [-11/20,19/20]. Thus

    M=1+3/2+1=7/2,
    k=2,
    max fiber length=3/2<M/k=7/4.                    (1)

There is no heavy fiber even for the occupied-parity budget.

## 2. Two actual minimizing caps at a globally deepest point

Let y=(0,1/10). Its raw mixed depth is exactly 33/20. To prove the
lower bound, first consider a through-point upper cap
x+a z>=1/10. Its middle length is 17/20. The endpoint thresholds
t_-,t_+ have sum 1/5. Their upper-tail lengths sum to at least 4/5:
if both are proper the sum is 1-(t_-+t_+)=4/5; if one is full it is
at least 1; if one is empty the other's length is at least 4/5 unless
it is already full. Both cannot be empty. Hence every upper cap has
mass at least 17/20+4/5=33/20.

For a through-point lower cap the middle contribution is 13/20.
The two endpoint LOWER thresholds again have sum 1/5. Their lower
tail lengths sum to at least 1: if neither is full, and both are
proper, their sum is 1+1/5>1; if one threshold is below -1/2, the
other exceeds 1/2 and is full. Thus the bound is 13/20+1=33/20.
Vertical caps containing the middle base have mass at least 5/2.
Shrinking a containing cap to the point shows these cases cover all
closed ambient halfspaces.

The two fixed caps

    H_+={x>=1/10},
    H_-={x-2z<=1/10}                                (2)

both attain 33/20. The first is proper on all three fibers. For the
second, the left fiber is strictly empty, the middle cut is proper,
and the right fiber is strictly full. No supporting-facet coincidence
occurs. Their restrictions cover the whole middle plane because there
they are the opposite inequalities x>=1/10 and x<=1/10. Thus they
bound every middle candidate above by 33/20. At an endpoint, each
own half-interval can be extended with a finite integer tilt excluding
the other two bounded fibers, so every endpoint point has depth at
most 1/2. Consequently

    max_(w in S) depth_S(w)=(33/20)/(7/2)=33/70.      (3)

Both caps are genuine global minima among caps through y. Their
continuous normals are +1,-1 and have positive balance. Their coarea
section masses, with continuous normals normalized to one, are
S_+=3 and S_-=1. The three sections of H_+ are (-1,1/10),(0,1/10),
(1,1/10), with full ambient mean y. H_- has only the middle section
y. Hence both have the full section-centroid stationarity identities,
including the integer-normal equation.

The usual circuit response weights are proportional to 1/S_+,1/S_-,
so kappa_+=1/4 and kappa_-=3/4. With beta=33/70 the corresponding
cap multipliers are

    lambda_+=35/66, lambda_-=35/22,
    lambda_++lambda_-=1/beta=70/33.                  (4)

They satisfy the exact original volume-budget identity
lambda_+ mu(H_+)+lambda_- mu(H_-)=M.

## 3. The actual convex own-depth hypograph changes both budgets

For an interval [L,U], its own raw depth at x is
f(x)=min(x-L,U-x). Here d=1, so the own-depth root is f itself.
The family

    C-hat={(z,x,r):(z,x) in C, 0<=r<=f_z(x)}

is a genuine compact convex body: f_z(x)=min(x-L(z),U(z)-x) is jointly
concave. Its integer fibers are triangles. Their areas are the squares
of the original interval lengths divided by four. Therefore its total
mixed two-dimensional volume is

    M-hat=1/4+9/16+1/4=17/16.                        (5)

Lift the ORIGINAL caps (2) vertically in r. Their volumes are integrals
of f_z over their original interval traces. In an endpoint fiber, the
H_+ integral is (1/2)(1/2-1/10)^2=2/25. In the middle fiber, the lower
piece up to 1/10 has integral
(1/2)(1/10+11/20)^2=169/800. The whole middle tent has area 9/16.
It follows exactly that

    mu-hat(H_+)=9/16-169/800+2(2/25)=409/800,
    mu-hat(H_-)=169/800+1/4=369/800.                  (6)

The original equal budgets have become unequal, with difference 1/20.
Their normalized lifted fractions are 409/850 and 369/850, whereas
both original fractions were 33/70. The ORIGINAL multipliers (4) give

    lambda_+ mu-hat(H_+)+lambda_- mu-hat(H_-)
       =2653/2640=M-hat-19/330.                      (7)

Thus even their total budget identity is not preserved by uniform
hypograph volume. No moving lift height of y changes (6), because
these lifted original caps are independent of r. New r-dependent
caps or a nonuniform measure would be a different construction whose
connection to the original cap family must be proved.

## 4. Surface stress has a separate singularity

For any full-dimensional convex continuous fiber K, its own depth
vanishes on boundary K: a supporting halfspace there has zero
d-dimensional volume. The graph lift of its original boundary is
therefore boundary K times {0}. This rim has H_d measure zero in
the (d+1)-dimensional hypograph, while original boundary stress is
measured by H_(d-1) and may have positive mass there. In this interval
example the original boundary consists of six endpoint atoms, whereas
their graph lifts are vertices of the three triangles and have zero
length. Consequently directly pushing the original surface stress
does not produce an absolutely continuous ordinary surface-area
stress on the hypograph. A singular rim law could be considered,
but it is not supplied by the usual surface-volume formula.

The volume obstruction (6)--(7) is stronger than this dimensional
observation: it occurs at actual globally deepest caps with full
section-centroid stationarity and no heavy fiber. It still does not
disprove a proposed transfer using additional shape-minimum information,
a proved nonuniform density, or a different explicitly tracked cap map.
The original family is safely above its OC constant 1/4, by (3).
